author: D

components.title: Split & normalize items
components.what: Handle the empty/whitespace-only string case returning [], split s on commas, strip whitespace from each item, and raise ValueError immediately if any resulting item is empty (e.g. '1,,2').

components.title: Parse each item as int or range
components.what: For each non-empty item, determine if it's a single integer or a 'a-b' range. Must correctly handle stripping whitespace around the '-' and around each sub-number, and must raise ValueError if either side is not a valid integer (e.g. '1.5', 'abc', '1-').

components.title: Validate semantics
components.what: Raise ValueError for negative integers (single or in a range), and for ranges where first > second. Must not confuse a leading minus sign (negative number) with the range-separator dash.

components.title: Build result
components.what: Expand ranges inclusively, collect all values, deduplicate, and return as a sorted list.

log.author: C

challenges.problem: It only accepts ASCII digits, so a leading-plus form such as "+2" is rejected. If “integer” includes standard signed integer syntax, this is incomplete; the draft should explicitly justify the stricter grammar or support an optional '+' while still rejecting negatives.

On Python 3.11+, int() raises ValueError for decimal strings exceeding the interpreter's digit-conversion limit, even though such a string consists solely of digits and denotes an integer. Thus the documented digit validation does not guarantee successful parsing for arbitrarily long valid integers.

A valid input such as '0-1000000000' causes collected.update(range(...)) to allocate roughly one billion set entries and can exhaust memory. The requested output itself is large, but the draft gives no guard or documented resource behavior.
